page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 server family. It is configured with 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The underlying hardware features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. This configuration consists of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core. The instance has a dedicated CPU allocation, does not include any bundled GPU hardware, and does not feature local storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-standard-4 primarily in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng CPU testing, both single-core and multi-core performance are categorized in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall within the bottom 10%, reflecting its positioning as an entry-tier general-purpose resource. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only small block cached speeds of 161.16 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds reach 24.13 GB/sec and 20.93 GB/sec respectively. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves an average text generation speed of 104.71 tokens per second when running a small 135M parameter language model, though prompt processing speeds remain in the bottom 25%.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the e2-standard-4 offers a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require high-performance compute or intensive storage I/O. The absence of local storage and GPUs, combined with its modest processing capabilities, makes it suitable for lightweight applications. Recommended workloads include basic web serving, small-scale database operations, development environments, and general-purpose utility tasks where resource density and budget considerations outweigh raw processing speed.
